sources.entry: bidict - Efficient, Pythonic bidirectional map data structures and related functionality.

summary.one_liner: bidict is a Python library providing efficient, Pythonic bidirectional mapping data structures that let you look up keys by value as well as values by key.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes bidict as the bidirectional mapping library for Python. It offers a dict-like bidirectional map where each value can be looked up back to its key through an inverse attribute, as shown in the quick start example mapping element symbols to names. The README says it has no runtime dependencies beyond Python's standard library and is fully type-hinted. It claims 100% test coverage across supported Python versions, including property-based tests and benchmarks. Documentation is hosted separately and linked from the README (intro, changelog, learning-from-bidict, contributors guide).
use_cases: map keys to values and values back to keys
maintain reverse index in Python programs
notable: No runtime dependencies beyond the Python standard library
Fully type-hinted and reported 100% test coverage
Listed in awesome-python under Built-in Classes Enhancement
Used by teams at Google, Venmo, CERN, Baidu and Tencent according to the README
caveats: Sole maintainer, per the README; community support is voluntary and enterprise support is a paid Tidelift or direct arrangement
Documentation links in the README may break on GitHub or PyPI, and the README points to alternate links for those cases
README does not state platform limits
